inlines.v: LA'ZY, adjective [Latin laxus, and it is doubtful whether this is of the same family.] 1. Disinclined to action or exertion; naturally or habitually slothful; sluggish; indolent; averse to labor; heavy in motion. Wicked men will ever live like rogues, and not fall to work, but be lazy and spend victuals. 2. Slow; moving slowly or apparently with labor; as a lazy stream. The night-owl's lazy flight.
